rows.text: The Nameless cannot turn a blind eye to evil.
For Firefly's sake, we must get to the bottom of all this.
Playing it safe seems to be the smarter move.
Can I toss a die to let it decide for me?
Did "Death" kill Robin?
Do you think this is connected to Acheron?
Have you noticed anything else unusual?
I don't have any other questions.
...Ah, friend. My expression wasn't much better than yours when I first saw this.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Your eyes aren't deceiving you — it's her, the famous singer Robin.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: But... how is that possible?
Could Robin actually...

First of all, can I just say that this had nothing to do with me. I'm just an unlucky bystander here. The Family can testify for me. If you don't believe me, just ask anyone in the Bloodhound Family — they hate me, and they hate the IPC, so they'd never lie.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: This is not where the crime happened. What I showed to you was a "memory" — the most basic Light Cone manifesting tech, authorized by the Garden of Recollection and owned by the IPC.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Did you really think the Galaxy Ranger was an outsider this whole time?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Penacony has made a solemn commitment to protect the safety of anyone inside a Family dream. Any person in distress will be forcibly awakened and safely returned to reality.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: What gives them the confidence to make such conclusive statements? Because behind this promise is the Harmony: The Family's Dreamweavers link up their minds together to construct an unbreakable defensive line.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Breaking through this line of defense to create "Death" in the dreamscape... Not even a Memokeeper could do that without The Family's permission.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Who could have done it? Friend, the only one is her, the girl who calls herself a Galaxy Ranger... An imposter, an unsought guest, an Emanator who hides her true identity...
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Ifrit's death was a foregone conclusion, and Robin... her misfortune was staring right at her. Who will be the next to die?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: This really is... hard to take in.
That's just one side of the story.
If that's the case, I can't trust anyone.
It's fine. Listen to your gut. Building trust always takes time, and I'm willing to wait.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: I just hope you realize that wherever that legacy is concerned... covert plans are already underway throughout Penacony. Everyone's got their own agenda.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Careful you don't get stuck on the wrong side. If I were you, I'd keep my distance from Acheron. After all, any schemes out in the open are always going to be better than a monster in the shadows... right?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Who's to say there isn't an even deeper conspiracy lurking beneath the surface?
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: ...Memokeeper, I think our little deal is finished.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: On the surface, this doesn't look like a bad deal for you. But Aventurine is a shrewd merchant whose scheme won't just be as simple as it appears to be.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: He doesn't know about Miss Firefly yet — but judging by your reaction, he may have noticed something going on and deliberately shifted topics to the "Truth of Death" to try and pull you in line with his way of thinking.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: That's quick thinking, and very sound logic. Aventurine is no fool. And working with him definitely has its dangers.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: The Nameless cannot turn a blind eye to evil.
But you're talking about REAL evil.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: For Firefly's sake, we must get to the bottom of all this.
That... is something I agree on.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Playing it safe seems to be the smarter move.
Insofar as things are presently concerned, yes. But what about the long-term?
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Anyway, be careful out there. There's more than one way to blaze a trail. In a dark forest beset by wolves ensuring your own escape to safety should be your primary concern.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: I'm not sure the two cases were committed by the same culprit, but that massive wound... looked like its winged blade. We've all witnessed it in action before.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Leaving it up to fate? It's just how that gambler thinks.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: As for the other questions...
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Did "Death" kill Robin?
Plus... it seems unlikely that there would be two lethal entities loose in the dreamscape.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Do you think this is connected to Acheron?
Sorry, I can't answer that question. That ranger is shrouded in mystery. I'm afraid no one is capable of providing an answer.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: But without a doubt... she is the most "special" guest at this banquet. It's like Aventurine said just then. It's best to keep your distance from her.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Have you noticed anything else unusual?
Two victims appearing one after the other in a very short time span... In and of itself, that's very unusual.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Two possibilities: The collapse of Penacony's Dreamscape has started speeding up, making "Death" extremely agitated and weakening The Family's protections. Or, everything has been planned out and executed by someone.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: If someone has chosen these victims deliberately... First a stowaway, then a Family celebrity... Then this murderer's motives are worth thoroughly chewing over.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: It's all happened so quickly I can only make conjecture. After leaving here, go have a chat with your companions. I hope you can clarify the source of this confusion.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Aventurine is telling the truth. This "memory" is a real one, and there's no sign of any distortion grafting on.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: The IPC is not the Garden, and there are real limits to what they can actually do. But you know all this.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Friend, let's not beat around the bush here — the thing is, I want to reach out personally to team up with the Astral Express.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: I told you, I'm just not interested in scrambling for "the Legacy." I just came to Penacony for work. I'm here to retrieve some lost property for the IPC, if you catch my drift... I'm talking ownership of this "frontier prison."
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: This has all become a bad debt thanks to the {RUBY_B#Stellaron}Cancer of All Worlds{RUBY_E#}. The IPC has tried sitting down for negotiations time and again, but The Family wouldn't even take our calls.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: You have no idea how difficult these people are to deal with. Put it this way — they've hushed up the existence of "Death" before, so they can definitely cover up any news about Robin's death.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: It'll just quietly float off like a bubble and pop, nobody ever being the wiser...
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: That's not fair, right? So then, friend, I need your help.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: I have but only one goal: The Family's front door is like a high wall, and to tear the whole thing down I'll have to dig out a few chunks first. Once I find a weak point, the IPC will have plenty of means.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Now we have our chance. So long as we can get to the truth behind her death, we can have justice for Robin while also gaining a valuable bargaining chip for bringing The Family to the table.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Truly a once-in-a-blue-moon opportunity... I've been investigating and making lots of friends all over Penacony precisely for this very moment.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: This tragic news would be extremely bad for The Family, so they'll be doing everything they can to stop it leaking — especially to the IPC.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: But I trust there are still a few factions that remain exceptions, and that's why I need you all. The reputation of the Astral Express precedes you, and the Harmony will give you the fairest of appraisals.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: You get to find out really what happened and seek justice, and I get to put it toward completing my mission for the IPC... It's what you call a win-win situation.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Don't worry. Just head back and talk things over with your companions.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: That navigator is really smart. She must understand the value of this deal. Look, here's my contact details. If you come to any conclusions, call me.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Oh, and... take this! A thorough investigation can always use a little more funding. Don't mention it!
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: So long, friend. I really am looking forward to uncovering the truth about "Death" with everyone.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: (Aventurine just sauntered off... He really doesn't mean to force it, but something still seems off...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: ...What now? What are your plans?
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: (Black Swan... What is she thinking?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: This way... This is where we part ways. All of this is like... a nightmare.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Unfortunately, the Remembrance doesn't lie... What we just saw is the "reality" that happened — and it won't fade from our minds just because we wake up.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: But follow your heart and don't be afraid. We all walk through this world casting shadows of different lengths, and ultimately... all we leave behind are precious memories.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: ...Welcome to this sad world, {RUBY_B#Child Blessed by Gaiathra}Kakavasha{RUBY_E#}.
...Ah, hold on just a sec.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: There you go, a small parting gift. If one day, you unfortunately fall into the deep waters of the Memory Zone and there's no Memokeeper to join you — hopefully it can guide you on my behalf.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: I also pay great attention to the ways of the world... Just think of this as an apology from me for hiding something from you.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Just as you guessed: Nobody outside knows about Robin's death, there aren't even baseless conspiracy theories. They're still streaming the rehearsal for her ceremony — using a stand-in, I guess — *ahem* they must be dreaming.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Of course. Who could imagine that death would actually descend upon the idyllic dream created by The Family, let alone that the victim would be the female lead of the Charmony Festival...
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: To be honest with you, I didn't believe it and even tested it a few times myself — until I discovered that I couldn't actually die. Whenever there's any danger, I'm forced awake by the Dreampool and it's all as if everything were just a nightmare.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Then... I've something private to take care of regarding that Galaxy Ranger. Let's leave things there, shall we?
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: What fascinating memories will you bring for me next time we meet...? I sincerely look forward to them.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: (A Family rep... Is Himeko okay...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Two murder cases!? I told you, something seemed off about the Nameless. {M#He}{F#She} must have come across the other one...
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: This murderer is a psycho... but I have to say, the case does represent an opportunity. We can leverage The Family's malfeasance and let the IPC use this as a reason to intervene.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: (So much has happened... I should take a moment to gather my thoughts, and wait for everyone to arrive...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: ...It appears the outcome has already been determined.
rows.speaker: Duke Inferno

rows.text: There are plenty of chips, but it'd be best to choose carefully. The most straightforward... has to be Robin. Remember? That Masked Fool once told me to find a mute as a friend.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: ...but she died, right before my very eyes.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: They're still alive, as are you.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: You still have room to make a choice. Leave the music box behind, and then go.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Choice? The bloody trail of the Destruction leaves no room for hesitation.
rows.speaker: Duke Inferno

rows.text: Fetora's fire demon... Even if you sacrifice your life for that Aeon, you won't get special treatment.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Ranger, you tread the narrow Path of The Hunt. You could never understand.
rows.speaker: Duke Inferno

rows.text: We come from the fire, and are born bathed in fire. We spread, burn, and destroy until all the kindling has burned out, and we leave only ashes on the ground.
rows.speaker: Duke Inferno

rows.text: Burning forms the entire life of a fire demon, from the beginning to the end. We are born to die, just to put into practice a profile of another universal truth: All things are created for the Destruction.
rows.speaker: Duke Inferno

rows.text: Your companions don't seem to think so. They fight for your chance at survival.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: They are my children and, just as I was, they are flames that have yet to burn white-hot. They're still young and I don't blame them.
rows.speaker: Duke Inferno

rows.text: Sunday.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: But my flames are faint and time is running out. Can you see the Planet of Festivities in the distance? I plan to bring purgatory with me there — and before that, I must surpass you.
rows.speaker: Duke Inferno

rows.text: Why?
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Because on the path THEY have forged, you have traveled farther than I have...
rows.speaker: Duke Inferno

rows.text: ..."Emanator."
rows.speaker: Duke Inferno

rows.text: Without any further ado, let's set off — lead the way! The show... is about to begin.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: A while ago...
You cannot hide your true identity. Draw that sword, for we shall indeed remain here, bound to fight a decisive battle to the death, for I choose this.
rows.speaker: Duke Inferno

rows.text: Destruction is intense but brief. To cravenly cling to life is to endure an endlessly prolonged existence.
rows.speaker: Duke Inferno

rows.text: Even if the answer... turns out to be your own destruction?
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: What's important is not the answer, but that it exists — just as you exist. Everything exists to be destroyed — Emanators are no different.
rows.speaker: Duke Inferno

rows.text: Black Swan gently touches the root of your ear, leaving a cool sensation. Then, she hands a card over to you.
I also pay great attention to the ways of the world... Just think of this as an apology from me for hiding something from you.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: That's it?
Just as even {RUBY_B#Penacony}sweet dreams{RUBY_E#} may be born of the void, the so-called impossible is merely something that has yet to happen.
rows.speaker: Duke Inferno

rows.text: Thank you.
...Alright. I accept.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: You shall witness the most brilliant and intense fire in existence. May this flame illuminate the farthest reaches of your bottomless dream.
rows.speaker: Duke Inferno

rows.text: A bottomless dream... Yes, that's right. But you've made one small mistake.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: This blade remains in its scabbard not out of pity or scorn. It's a personal secret that I don't want to disclose, but perhaps out of reciprocity...
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: You had no desire to kill [Trailblazer]. You only did what you did to drive me and the Memokeeper away... But why?
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: ...I'll reveal the truth to you.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: The Hunt... is not the path I truly follow.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: May death be the end of your boundless dream...
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: ...guiding you back to the waking world.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: ..."My time"?
rows.speaker: Sam

rows.text: I've seen many clever disguises that can conceal appearances, but they can never cover up who a person really is. And you're no different.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Did Destiny's Slave make you do it?
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: You know Elio.
rows.speaker: Sam

rows.text: I thought this is just the kind of thing that'd get written into your "script."
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: My "script" has always been brief. Other than that. Anything beyond that is unnecessary.
rows.speaker: Sam

rows.text: He knows my nature: There is but a single destiny, from which no one can escape... And until then, I hold the privilege of choice.
rows.speaker: Sam

rows.text: However, you appear to be ignorant of this, so it's time for me to inquire: Who exactly are you?
rows.speaker: Sam

rows.text: Not your enemy, perhaps.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: That's not what I asked.
rows.speaker: Sam

rows.text: I don't deserve your curiosity. Loners wandering the cosmos always have their secrets. Take me. I've also been wanted by the IPC, so it's little wonder I know something about the Stellaron Hunters... that's all.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Maybe I can help.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: What reason would you have for doing that?
rows.speaker: Sam

rows.text: I tend to forget things — which is why, rather than memories, I'm accustomed to using my emotions to capture what I normally wouldn't otherwise. So...
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: ...I know who is inside that cold armor.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: How about it? Ready to take off that armor and sit down for a talk?
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: What's next, then? [Trailblazer]'s been taken by Black Swan. Will you go look for {M#him}{F#her}?
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: It's not yet time.
rows.speaker: Sam

rows.text: I don't need help, but I can give you a suggestion that would make things better for you and me.
rows.speaker: Sam

rows.text: If your goal is the Watchmaker's Legacy, then go look into The Family. Not only are they covering up the existence of "Death," but they're burying the past and the truth about what happens inside the Dreamscape.
rows.speaker: Sam

rows.text: Already on it.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: ...and the Astral Express is no enemy of yours.
rows.speaker: Sam

rows.text: I know that... I just never expected to hear you say it.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: No need for that... No harm in mentioning that Elio's only given me one instruction: "Get all of the Astral Express to track down the grand legacy."
rows.speaker: Sam

rows.text: I tried settling this in an easier and more direct way, but as you can see, here I am, confronting you: I failed. Can't ever go against "the script."
rows.speaker: Sam

rows.text: "The so-called impossible is merely something that has yet to happen"...
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: ...That's it. Before we split, can I ask you one more thing?
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Is there anything else in your "script" about me? I'd like to know what kind of footnote "I" get to leave in that future foreseen by destiny?
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Unfortunately, not a thing came up.
rows.speaker: Sam

rows.text: ...I knew it.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Hang on...
rows.speaker: Sam

rows.text: I don't.
rows.speaker: Sam

rows.text: Don't what?
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Black Swan leads you through the chaotic Dreamscape...
Some time ago — Deep in Memory Zone
Days ago — Ever-Flame Mansion
Present day — Golden Hour
Your first question was: "Do you still have dreams about everyone who died because of you?"
rows.speaker: Sam

rows.text: I don't. Never have.
rows.speaker: Sam

rows.text: I was born without the ability to "dream." I live for this cold harsh reality, for a little light, and to burn... to keep on burning, until I turn to ash.
rows.speaker: Sam

rows.text: So, I really envy you.
rows.speaker: Sam

rows.text: Is that so...
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Then you're already living in the waking world.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: We heard about Miss Firefly from Black Swan... But we never expected Miss Robin to...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'm sorry... that I couldn't be with you then.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Reality cruises on in serenity, while undercurrents bubble up from the Dreamscape... just like that Memokeeper said...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: ...Stay strong, everyone. We can still do what we can for them... starting with finding the murderer.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Let's recap everything then. [Trailblazer] just reminded me of something: March, do you remember what that Family rep who negotiated with us said?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: "Indeed, we trust that the Nameless has nothing to do with this, and we also beg each of you to help assist The Family in verifying the identity of the deceased." That's how it was put... in reference to Miss Firefly.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Looking back, he seemed a little evasive at the time. And he also failed to mention anything about the earlier murder, too.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The Family is planning on covering up all news about Miss Robin's death. If news gets out, Penacony is going to turn into a bloodbath...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: But the murder that followed closely after was obviously beyond their anticipation. The Family had to try and turn things to their advantage by bringing in reinforcements from outside. The Charmony Festival is nearly here — they must be snowed under.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: It may also be that Miss Firefly's murder had so many witnesses that it couldn't be covered up, so they went with the flow and let more people on the scene to control the situation.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: After all, the nature of the two murders is fundamentally different... The Family's first protective measures should be against malicious actors among the guests, such as that IPC envoy.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: He really is up to no good.
Aventurine is on guard against Acheron.
All the while accusing that Galaxy Ranger...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Indeed, he was particularly concerned about that Galaxy Ranger.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Are we missing the forest for the trees here...? I always felt that Aventurine's reasons for accusing Miss Acheron were highly subtle. Can we believe him?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: At this point, I'm afraid the only ones we can trust are ourselves.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Look, let's try to gather intel first and then list all the possible outcomes we can. Then we go through them, eliminating contradictions one-by-one. The fewer facts remaining, the closer we are to the truth.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: She says this as her hand gently rests on the hilt of the sword.
...I've still got this sense of foreboding. It's like we're stuck in a whirlpool — spinning around that Legacy even after everything that's happened...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: This time we're playing the role of a real detective... But before we start, what are we going to say to The Family and Aventurine?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: As I see things, The Family harbors no ill-will towards the Astral Express — if they didn't trust the Crew, they wouldn't have casually commissioned outsiders to investigate a case that's in all likelihood "a scandal."
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Plus, this is The Family's turf. Teaming up with them should make things easier for us in the future.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: As for that Aventurine... Welt, I'd like to hear your thoughts.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: That's fine. I'm not forcing you.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: That's fine. I'm not forcing you.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: He's complex. He deliberately slow-played his hand during negotiations while running circles round us all the while.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Anyway, be careful out there. There's more than one way to blaze a trail. In a dark forest beset by wolves ensuring your own escape to safety should be your primary concern.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: I'm not sure the two cases were committed by the same culprit, but that massive wound... looked like its winged blade. We've all witnessed it in action before.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: It's all happened so quickly I can only make conjecture. After leaving here, go have a chat with your companions. I hope you can clarify the source of this confusion.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: He appealed convincingly to both reason and emotion. It wasn't forced, but the intent was obvious.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Still, it's good to have contacts among all this uncertainty. Aventurine showed his skills, and as far as our interests are aligned, he can become a reliable ally.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: We also need to keep a certain distance from The Family — never let them get too close. Teaming up with the IPC helps balance that out — if either side makes a move, we have the option to pull out.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: So you suggest accepting Aventurine's proposal to team up?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Yes... It's risky, but we can only wait until both sides have played their cards before making any further judgments.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I get why, but there's a whole lot of bad guys and girls around here and I'm worried about getting stabbed in the back. [Trailblazer] has been bullied a few times now, and I can't stand it anymore...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You're like a broken record...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Forget about it. Just let me keep an eye on him! If that doesn't work, we can just turn the tables and use him instead!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: But I'm really not asking for much, so why don't you at least hear me out, okay?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: But I'm really not asking for much, so why don't you at least hear me out, okay?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Then [Trailblazer], could you please reply to Aventurine? Everyone, take this time to put together your thoughts.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: (Looks like Aventurine is happy with this outcome... Let's tell everyone about it.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: An attack on the hotel guests? Unlikely. Penacony's guests include quite a few big wigs known throughout the whole cosmos, people who not even the IPC would dare take lightly. Aventurine is a shrewd merchant, and there's no way he doesn't know that.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: He's definitely going for The Family, and it's just a matter of how. The Harmony is strong in Penacony and almost impossible to take on head-to-head. The fact that the IPC dispatched Aventurine shows that they do not intend to simply play by the book here.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Aventurine has devoted considerable attention to her. But this Galaxy Ranger... we know hardly anything about her and can't rush to any conclusions.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: ...I was also considering this possibility, especially... because he respects you so much, and has sought you out before a few times. Perhaps he's also unsure of your intentions, and is probing you.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: ...I'm just speculating. In any case, we have to be careful when handling Aventurine. He's skilled at reading people and discerning the right moment to strike. Also...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Maybe Aventurine's goal was never to gain our trust. Maybe he wanted to foster a feeling of enmity toward Acheron and make the situation more volatile... Two birds, one stone.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: ...That fits the stereotype of a Galaxy Ranger to a T.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: No no, after all they've brought everyone this sleepy dreamscape which everyone loves. I just feel like I'm starting to understand them less and less...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Yeah! Of course, at times like this we're so lucky to have our Crew. The Family and the IPC — everyone has their own plans going on...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Black Swan gently touches the root of your ear, leaving a cool sensation. Then, she hands a card over to you.
Everyone's still having a great time out there on the streets. Nobody knows what's happened... It's all so unreal, as if Firefly, Miss Robin, and us... were all outsiders from another world.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Looks like Aventurine doesn't need anything else — let's turn our attention to The Family's assignment for now. Himeko, what do you think?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Among our current clues, the two murders that [Trailblazer] witnessed are the most directly connected. I suggest starting here.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: One thing I'm curious about is, if a person dies in a dream, what happens to them in real life? Seeing as we're at The Family's behest, why not pop back out to reality and verify Miss Firefly's situation back at the hotel... Perhaps we could also make a few inquiries about Miss Robin while we're out there.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: How about we split off into two groups? There are still some things worth focusing on inside the Dreamscape — I'll investigate those and we can link up again later.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Worth focusing on? ...Oh, no problem. I'll leave it to you then.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Huh? Ah... I thought I'd finally get to see Himeko and Mr. Yang go out on a mission together. Oh well, take care then, Mr. Yang!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I will. Keep in touch.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Honored guest, could you come out for a second?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I'd be embarrassed too, getting stared at like that.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Forgive me. My name is Welt Yang — I'm one of the Crew Members on the Astral Express. I believe you've met my colleagues.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Welt...
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: ...Is there something about my name?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: ...First, don't you want to know my name?
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: I already do, Miss Acheron. You're a prominent figure in Penacony.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: ...What are they saying about me?
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Some claim that you're the real culprit behind these murders... that the Annihilation Gang's tragic fate at the banquet was a result of your blade... and that you're now attempting to unleash another bloodbath on Penacony.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: The Annihilation Gang?
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Ifrit of Ever-Flame Mansion.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: "Tragic fate"... That duke turned his dying body to flames and sacrificed his life as a martyr. He was a determined and heroic Pathstrider. Not even a villain should be disparaged like this.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: And what's more, there were plenty of suspects invited. Do they really think... that a blade is more dangerous than that "black hole" you're wielding?
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: ...Keen intuition. Not even The Family managed to point out the truth behind this cane.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: So you must surely know, Miss Acheron, that peering into a black hole is not a wise move. As a potential threat, your knowledge of us has reached uncomfortable depths...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Reveal your true identity and intentions... Otherwise, brace yourself for gravitational disintegration.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: That shouldn't be necessary... but if it makes the Nameless feel less defensive, I'll be happy to abide.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Believe it or not, Galaxy Ranger, Acheron... those are the names I go by to this very day. My trip to Penacony is solely to fulfill an old "final request."
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: I'm here for the Watchmaker's Legacy... and that's it. I think I've been honest enough.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Still unwilling to reveal your true identity?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: It's not that I don't want to. It's just that I can't... I've come so far, and I can't sum up all of that in just a few words.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Everyone has their own unspeakable past, secrets that they don't want to be revealed... and I won't be asking any more questions, such as why the Astral Express is roaming around the cosmos with a Stellaron on board.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: [Trailblazer]'s fine. Let's stick with the topic. Gaining my trust all depends on how much you're willing to reveal.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I've run around many different Penacony dreamscapes just to try and find that "Legacy," and during this period I came into contact with quite a few guests. In the process, I gradually came to realize...
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: The secret of Penacony... may be closely related to the Trailblaze.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: That's why I've come to ask for your help. I don't have enough proof yet, but I'd like to speculate something: the source of all tragedy lies within The Family. If you could trust me... we could find the proof to support this claim, together.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Mr. Yang, I think you've come to the same conclusion, haven't you?
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: ...Let's leave it at that. For now, I'll choose to believe that you bear no hostility.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Share your findings with me, and me alone. I don't want vague conjecture to interfere with other people's judgments before we find solid proof.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Mhmm.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: ...By the way, would you like something to drink? Before we go, how about two cups of Wake the Heck Up...? No, four cups.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Because the conversation coming up... will last forever.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: I've been watching her closely for a while now, and the first "invitation" was in the banquet hall of the hotel.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: She just sat in one corner keeping silent, chugging down a couple cups of Wake the Heck Up... I told her it's a pungent, bitter beverage, not the taste of sweet dreams — only for people allergic to SoulGlad. And she said...
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: "Really? But I don't taste... any difference at all between them."
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Is {M#he}{F#she} okay? That Memokeeper... didn't do anything, right?
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: The guest rooms are charmingly minimalist...
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: ...An aesthetic you share, Miss Acheron.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: It's a cinch. This music box — the "invitation" received by the Annihilation Gang... There are latent memories that linger on it yet.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: You see, memories of you are not yours alone. They travel in other people... Other things. I know much, and I can predict even more. With some help, the dead can be made to speak.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: The Annihilation Gang, that band of desperadoes who all disappeared after meeting you... What exactly happened to them? Well, let me reveal all.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: "...Gradation twelve ██ Dreamscape twelve ██ Father ██ I dedicate this to you..."
rows.speaker: Voice in the Memory

rows.text: "...Well done ██ Dubra ██ wherever they go, ██ shall be met by annihilation..."
rows.speaker: Voice in the Memory

rows.text: ...There it is — it's hazy, but it's Ifrit's voice. The other one... is probably his progeny.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: This is the residual memory from when the 'invitation' was first delivered... they were abruptly interrupted. Then, what happened next is...
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: "...They sought refuge in the land of sleep ██, merely wishing for undisturbed rest, away from the storms..."
rows.speaker: Voice in the Memory

rows.text: "Children of the flame ██ this marks your rite of passage."
rows.speaker: Voice in the Memory

rows.text: "She won't be necessary ████ I alone am enough."
rows.speaker: Voice in the Memory

rows.text: The Ever-Flame Mansion has set out on a journey. Those poor people... They have no idea what lies in wait ahead of them.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Memory recovery is going well, but slowly. She'll be here soon, and time is short.... There's nobody else here, so there's no need to be delicate... In fact I think I'd better go all out....
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: ...What happened?
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: The memory after that... is blank? How is that possible... This music box fell into Acheron's hands, and she brought it to Penacony — that's a fact, and that's how it should have gone... but along the way...
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: ...It's like it's been erased? Who's done this...
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: "...Who are you?"
rows.speaker: Voice in the Memory

rows.text: No — is this not a "memory"?
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: "Oh... a Memokeeper. Do you serve the Garden of Recollection... or The Cremators?"
rows.speaker: Voice in the Memory

rows.text: Shh—████ when have those ██ on the Path of Destruction ██ feared death?
rows.speaker: Voice in the Memory

rows.text: "My name is Constance... A pleasure to meet you. We were supposed to meet in Penacony and spend an... unforgettable time together."
rows.speaker: Voice in the Memory

rows.text: "But that seems unrealistic. Dahlia's not welcome on the Banquet Star, and I don't need a coming-of-age ceremony... And you, I know what you're looking for..."
rows.speaker: Voice in the Memory

rows.text: "Want 'her' secret? I can give it to you, and then... you can enjoy the banquet for me."
rows.speaker: Voice in the Memory

rows.text: "I wish you 'unforgettable' memories."
rows.speaker: Voice in the Memory

rows.text: ...A phone? Want to listen in?
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: "A few days ago, the IPC made an announcement..."
rows.speaker: Interastral Peace Broadcast

rows.text: "Under the watchful guidance of the Marketing Development Department and in accordance with the Interstellar Peace Charter, the independent Sigonian Sovereignty has hereby been established, and shall take a legislative seat at the Interstellar Congress..."
rows.speaker: Interastral Peace Broadcast

rows.text: "The formation of the Sigonian Sovereignty is of great historical significance to the Sigonia system: This move puts an end to the planet's long and bloody history, turning the sensational Katica-Avgin Extinction Event into a distant memory..."
rows.speaker: Interastral Peace Broadcast

rows.text: "Sigonia-IV is located in an unclaimed zone at the intersection of the Dnies, Pruthian, and Dorneau star clusters. The planet's surface environment is known for being extremely harsh, constantly faced with the threat of impact from small-scale celestial objects..."
rows.speaker: Interastral Peace Broadcast

rows.text: "This is why very few intelligent species have made this planet their home. Dividing themselves into several tribes to eke out nomad lifestyles as they struggle to survive the arid desert wilderness, they have developed their own folk beliefs that are independent of the Aeon belief system..."
rows.speaker: Interastral Peace Broadcast

rows.text: ...Sigonia, Sigonia. Ravenous eye of the storm, spurned by all the gods...
Land of rock, but not water, lightning, but not rain, blood, but not tears. You beat us with your falling stars, you lash us with wind and storm, you chew us up with the cracked earth...

You promised us a land of {RUBY_B#Avgin}honey{RUBY_E#}, yet yoked us beneath a {RUBY_B#Katica}sword{RUBY_E#} of bitterness. O, {RUBY_B#Fenge Biyos}Gaiathra Triclops{RUBY_E#}, if Thou can hear me, please open up thy three eyes and gaze upon this child...
When you took his father, my child was still sleeping in my belly. And where my husband went, I too soon must go...

I don't ask for a peaceful death, just for you to tell me — does the baby swaddled sweetly asleep... does he dream of his mother's heartbeat and the sound of falling rain? Please tell me whether this life is all just a fleeting dream...
...Otherwise, why would this child be born to face impending death...?
Mommy...! Mommy...!
Mommy...! The rain — it's raining!
Raining...? Raining...
You...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It is raining! It's true! Those outworlders weren't lying to us. They really did summon the rain... Mommy, we can leave here... We can go back home!
Back home... Ahh... Gaiathra Triclops, you came. Do you hear that? Thank you... Thank you...
Darling, listen... this is the sound of rain. On the day you were born, the sky also sent down {RUBY_B#Raindrops}a gift{RUBY_E#} like this from Gaiathra.
Such a lucky child, such a blessed child... Just like your name. A gift from THEM to Avgin... my boy...
"May the goddess Gaiathra close her eyes three times..."
"Keep your blood eternally pulsing..."
"Let your journey be forever peaceful... "
"...and your schemes forever concealed."
Time to wake up, gambler.
Oh heavens, I must have drunk too much SoulGlad... Didn't expect you to be back so soon. How is it... find anything?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Present day — Golden Hour
That's why I'm convinced that there are a few big secrets lurking behind the scenes.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Then you must have heard about the {RUBY_B#"Something Unto Death"}Memory Zone meme{RUBY_E#} — when I graciously deigned to establish connections with the Oak Family on your behalf, they were quite in a pitiful state of disarray.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Besides Robin, there was another body. I don't know the exact details, just that it was a stowaway.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: It's just that their trickery runs deeper than I thought. Robin's stand-in was all ready to go... These two murders are definitely getting hushed up.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: What should we do? Let me think... It's too rare an opportunity to miss out on, so I gotta be careful...
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Incredible, gambler. Have you already exhausted your limited repertoire of tricks so soon?
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Robin is what she calls the "mute." She has lost her voice and while most people can't pick up on it, you and I cannot mistake that sound — not produced by any voicebox, but rather by the resonance of the Harmony.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: If that girl hadn't gone hoarse from singing practice, there'd only be one possibility: Something was up with The Family, or Robin herself. To get to the bottom of this, I tried every way I could to meet her...
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: A complete and utter loss — incidentally, it seems to have resulted in your rather undignified arrival on the interrogation stand.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: There were eyewitnesses at the scene, and The Family, in their graciousness, has tentatively accepted your alibi. However, for the foreseeable future... you shall, regrettably, find yourself under the vigilant watch of the Hounds.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Things aren't looking too optimistic, Doctor. I'm starting to break out in a cold sweat. Do you reckon... there's still any chance of a comeback given how things are?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: ...No! I can't accept this!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...No! I can't accept this!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: A probability? Yes, it exists, but it verges on the infinitesimal. To phrase it in a manner more befitting the vernacular of Penacony, "you're dreaming."
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: But if you simply can't control yourself and want to try your hand, then there just so happens to be a suitable candidate...
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: That man wants to see you again.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Who?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: ...Is this a public hearing, or a private trial?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: If it were the former, it would hardly befit my stature to stoop to the role of a mere messenger.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Fine... That's great. It's all great. You see, the dead can't talk — but the living can...
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Ratio, I'm convinced now that there must be something wrong inside The Family. Just you wait and see, that man's sister has died. He can't sit on his hands.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: At the same time — Hotel in the real world
At this moment, on the other side...
We're here. The Dewlight Pavilion is the Oak Family's fortress and a place where heads of the families meet to discuss great plans for Penacony.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Fortress? I like this metaphor. I had dealt with the warlords of the Iymanika star system not long ago, and their synchronized orbital manor wasn't this heavily guarded.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: This mansion nominally belongs to Sunday, and is very befitting of its owner. Without his express invitation, the likes of ordinary guests would never grace these grounds in their lifetimes. Look around while you still have this moment of freedom.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Hey, Doc — Whose side are you on anyway?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Quite a fascinating contraption. I would rate it more favorably if that clamorous little person inside were gone.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Ratio... I can hear you...
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Who's to say I won't sell you out?
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: We'll see. When we meet the {RUBY_B#Sunday}authoritarian master{RUBY_E#} of the Oak Family, I'll pry an answer out of him.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Follow me, and I'll bring you to his parlor. Hold your tongue and let me deal with the members of The Family.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: ...A dead end?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: The door is shut tight. Looks like we're on our own.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: I mean... there isn't a door. How did you get in before?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: For security reasons, The Family built the administrative site deep in the Dreamscape, with the mechanisms hidden in these Nightingale statues. The direction of the statues can be controlled.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: On the previous occasion, an attendant named Conna had gone to the side room to verify something before setting the statues in the correct positions.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Maybe we should do the same. Let's go and take a look. Of course, we can also use brute force.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Six Nightingales facing in different directions — an obvious hint.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Hmm... but are these Nightingales?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: They are. What's wrong?
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: How can Nightingales be so huge? They look more like Torment Eagles to me.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: There are no eagles in the Five Families, only Nightingales— Why am I wasting time with you on this?
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Just as I thought, here's the correct answer.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: A truly miraculous discovery — perhaps I should offer you the chance to join the Genius Society?
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Really? I thought you'd given up on that already.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: I was being sarcastic. Can't you tell?
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Solving a problem by brute force doesn't prove your intelligence. The side room — don't let me repeat myself.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Look, like I said — brute force can also solve things.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: The Council of Mundanites should consider you as their member, for no one in this universe is more suitable to be there than you.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Impressive. So much for Mr Sunday's reserved, virtuous image.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Do you need me to remind you? We're in a dreamscape. No matter how grand the mansion looks, it'll not affect Penacony. Stop wasting your time nitpicking The Family here.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Yeah, you're right. The only way to destroy The Family is "Death." Sunday must have thought the same. Let's head down.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: ...Hold on.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: What's wrong? Are we heading the wrong way?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Yes.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: No, but this door is locked.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: My friend, did you really make an appointment with him?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Yes.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: ...It's a trial. You got to prove your worth to Sunday before you can speak with him.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Yes.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: If I'm not wrong, we need to find a way to open this door in the hall, or this place will be our prison.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Yes.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Oh, an escape room — my favorite.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Yes.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Get serious. I've no time for games. Let's head back. The hint is probably in that prominent sandpit.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Let's look around. When I see it, I will know it.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Fine, fine. Why do I feel that we're pursuing a degree in burglary now?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Found it. This is it.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: The nameplate reads: Gulliver's Arch. I'm amazed you can remember something this tiny. You know, this reminds me of a tunnel I once saw that could shrink people who passed through it.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Yes.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: If I were you, I would shut my mouth. It's wise to remain silent when you should.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: This reminds me of one of those building toys. With the blocks? I've never played with them before. I wonder if it's more interesting than stacking chips.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Look, the gap is closed, and it fits perfectly — eh, so what's next?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: ...Good heavens. Did I shrink? Am I still in a dream?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Indeed.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Doctor... you're huge! It's me! Down here in the sandpit!
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Actually I think we could make this work for us. Just find a way to slip me into Sunday's collar, and I'll infiltrate The Family just like that.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Fine. I was just kidding.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Let's find a way to open the door.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Hello. Welcome to the Golden Hour base model.
rows.speaker: Oak Family Soldier

rows.text: I am an Oak Soldier. I will be here to guide you through the tour of the base model. Happy to be of service.
rows.speaker: Oak Family Soldier

rows.text: Then tell me about the tour.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Hel—l—l—l—l—o. Welcome to the Golden Hour ba—a—a—a—a—se model —
rows.speaker: Oak Family Soldier

rows.text: I am an O—o—o—o—o—oak Soldier. I will be here to guide you through the to—o—o—o—ur of the base mo —
rows.speaker: Oak Family Soldier

rows.text: Model. Happy to be of service.
rows.speaker: Oak Family Soldier

rows.text: Gen—n—n—n—n—n—nerating guide. Please wait pa—a—a—a—a—a—atient—t—t—t...
rows.speaker: Oak Family Soldier

rows.text: t-t-t-t-t...
rows.speaker: Oak Family Soldier

rows.text: ...Fo—o—o—o—und the nearest check-in spot!
rows.speaker: Oak Family Soldier

rows.text: Please lo—o—o—o—ok behind me — a capsule m—a—a—a—a—chine model—
rows.speaker: Oak Family Soldier

rows.text: Mode-e-e-e-e-e-e-l—
rows.speaker: Oak Family Soldier

rows.text: What's up with that? Now The Family's toys are trying to frame me? I didn't do a thing to it, Doc. You've gotta be my witness.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: I saw nothing.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Capsule machine... There's no mechanism on the floor. Could there be one at the top? Doctor, do me a favor —
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: So I was right. These models have interiors that look exactly like the real buildings. The only difference is that no one lives in them.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Funny that Sunday puts a miniature that makes him seem like a giant by comparison right where he can see it first thing in the morning. Insecure much?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Doctor... Shake a leg...?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Without that Pinball machine, neither one of us is going anywhere anytime soon.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Ha, you're back! Just place it here... Thank you...!
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Place the model in the sandpit.
Ratio, you should come in and take a look. The view here is breathtaking. Honestly, you could easily squash me with just a pinch.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: If that is your wish, I will do so without a moment's hesitation.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: And the joyous tour of Toy City has come to an end. It makes me feel sad.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Penacony isn't all bad, right? I'll use this interesting experience as a talking point at the poker table.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: It's a pity you made it out of the sandpit alive. Sunday is just beyond this door. From my limited understanding, he's not someone easily handled. Are you prepared?
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Yeah, only I believe he's the one who should be prepared to face me.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Tell me about your plan.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: I don't have a plan. I'll just play it by ear. There are only two kinds of bargaining chips when dealing with people: Benefit or fear.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Looks like "sincerity" isn't in your dictionary.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Am I not sincere enough? There's no need to emphasize it. We've got to make good use of death. That man's sister is dead. He won't be able to turn a blind eye, and that's "fear."
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: And I'll help him find the murderer. He can't do it due to his status and position, but I can, and that's "benefit."
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: On what basis do you believe he's incapable, necessitating the delegation to someone from a rival faction, the IPC?
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Simple — Because that murderer could very well be a traitor hiding inside The Family.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: ...Do you mean the Galaxy Ranger whom you accused previously?
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: That was just an excuse, good doctor. There's something wrong with that woman, and we need someone to keep her in check. It's better to minimize the variables outside of our control when we execute our plans.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Moreover, I need to know her identity. If I'm lucky, she could be an important pawn. And it's good to have more helpful friends when dealing with this matter.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: But honestly, the murder case is likely unrelated to her. I believe my standpoint: There's a rat in The Family. Otherwise, why would Mr. Sunday arrange a private meeting with us? This isn't an interrogation, but a secret negotiation.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: We'll see. Using Robin's death as a bargaining chip, I'll win back my freedom and power. In the end, I'll ruin this beautiful dream and create the grandest death.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: If the chance of winning is just beyond this door, even if that chance is close to zero, well... you can't win if you don't play, right?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Ah, the charming audacity! To think that you, of all people, might emerge victorious, dear gambler.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Three chips are enough.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: All or nothing.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: It seems my puzzles are too effortless for you, IPC Ambassador.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I appreciate your words, and I see you put a lot of effort into welcoming me, Mr. Sunday. However, this is no way to greet a guest.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Well, this isn't an invitation, but a summoning. Before we speak, I need to test your character.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I imagine this knowledgeable doctor friend of yours has been of great help, yes?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Certainly, you ought to know this better than I do — he has already faithfully fulfilled his duties, hasn't he?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Yes, the doctor has assured me of your noble character. He considers you, like himself, a virtuous person who can be trusted by The Family.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I have come to know you very well as a person, Mr. Aventurine. You're diligent, generous, and willing to cooperate. The fact that you succeeded in overcoming many obstacles just to meet me gave me the reason to believe in your wisdom and courage.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: But there's one thing I must ask you — that is, you've used your wisdom at the wrong place to meet the wrong person and put yourself in a situation where you shouldn't be... witnessing a {RUBY_B#Robin's Case}tragedy{RUBY_E#} that shouldn't have happened.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: You don't look too well. Am I making you anxious?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: ...If not, then it means I'm on your side.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: If I wasn't mistaken, you'd just made a serious accusation against The Family.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: You weren't mistaken, for depravity is creeping in around you.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: There's no need for us to be evasive. Let's talk about your sister. Your sister's talent is unrivaled in the world of show business. As you know, her voice has been out of tune since she returned to Penacony. What's more disheartening, she {RUBY_B#Death}can't sing anymore{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Who could be responsible for this? Many suspect the culprit is among the outsiders, but I know... you hold a different opinion.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Now, your noble status has become a shackle, preventing you from apprehending the murderer and avenging your sister's death. You're feeling anxious because you're out on a limb.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: But don't worry. I am on your side.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: I'm immensely honored by your concern for me, Mr. Aventurine — since you're so selfless and generous, I believe you wouldn't ask for anything in return, would you?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Naturally, you wouldn't incur any loss from this. I just want to reclaim what is mine: My liberty, and the personal items under The Family's custody — the bag of gift money, and...
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: The box in which the Cornerstone is stored.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: That's right.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Cornerstone — I've heard it's a treasured asset of the Strategic Investment Department, a sacred stone that seals the "Preservation" Emanator, granting significant power, and every {RUBY_B#Ten Stonehearts}Liquidation Specialist{RUBY_E#} holds one.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: ...For an object so precious, it probably comes at an even higher price than other forms of recompense.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I'm sure you're aware of the high level of risk I'll be undertaking to bring the truth to light.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Mr. Aventurine, when you're out and about, do you always make adjustments to your appearance? Your tie should be on the center line, your shirt must not protrude from your vest, your trouser creases should be perfectly straight, and always aligned with the tips of your shoes.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Waaaaaah...!
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Of course.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: But I don't, because it's not appropriate to do so in public — you should make sure everything is presentable and in order before leaving the house.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I'm not the kind that takes risks. The Cornerstone must be in the custody of The Family.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: No room for negotiation?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Please don't let me turn you down twice.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: ...Sure. The gift money is good enough. I suppose you wouldn't mind that? After all, a merchant can't function without a bargaining chip.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: You compromised quicker than I thought. Unfortunately, it's a gambler that needs a bargaining chip... not a merchant. I can give you your gift money, but before that, I want you to tell me —
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: — The fact that you can decisively forsake the box you asked for, what exactly is stored in it?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "Oh, Triple-Faced Soul, please sear his tongue and palms with a hot iron, so that he will not be able to fabricate lies and make false vows."
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: ...What have you done?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Under the light of the Harmony, all wickedness is revealed. I implore THEM to shed THEIR light, and I'll ask you questions on THEIR behalf. Next... you have 113 seconds to prove your innocence and gain my trust.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: And if I refuse to answer?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: You can try — and we'll see if the Harmony rejects you.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "Question: Do you own a Cornerstone?"
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: What a simple answer. You, too, understand that idle chatter leads only to poverty.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "Did you hand over the Cornerstone to The Family when you entered Penacony?"
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "Does the Cornerstone you handed over to The Family belong to you?"
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "Is your Cornerstone in this room right now?"
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "Is your memory free from any kind of tampering or deletion, encompassing but not restricted to the techniques of the Garden of Recollection?"
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "Are you an Avgin from Sigonia?"
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Yes. You even know about that?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: "Do the Avgins have any ability to read, tamper with, or manipulate one's own or another's mind?"
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: No. Does it matter?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: "Do you love your family more than yourself?"
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "All the Avgins were killed in a massacre. Am I right?"
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: No.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: "Are you your clan's sole survivor?"
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: ...Perhaps.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: "...Do you hate and wish to destroy this world with your own hands?"
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: ...Of course.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Looks like we can get an answer.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Open it, Mr. Aventurine... It's your last chance to defend your honor.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Since you came as promised, learned Doctor... Does this mean that you are willing to take the side of The Family in this farce?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: What makes you think you can convince me?
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: I've heard you haven't enjoyed Mr. Aventurine's company. I also understand that you're an avid learner who sees the pursuit of knowledge above all.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: In that case, you ought to realize that a competent scholar knows their position and wouldn't forsake more vital matters for the sake of petty pride.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: If you agree to assist The Family, I'll share our research findings on the Stellaron. You must be quite aware that, besides The Family, no other faction is willing to share such information.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: The two return on the path they came from...
Cut to the chase. What do you need from me?
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: I need Mr. Aventurine's comprehensive plan.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Haven't you confiscated his Cornerstone? You can't expect a featherless bird to take flight.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: But I've also heard the {RUBY_B#Ten Stonehearts}ten elites{RUBY_E#} in the Strategic Investment Department have united, progressing together in the interests of the IPC.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: You'll have to speak more clearly than that.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: The Cornerstone which Mr. Aventurine surrendered — was it really his?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: You question whether he would entrust you with someone else's Cornerstone? The Ten Stonehearts aren't as united as you think — Cornerstones are significantly more precious to them than their very own lives.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: But you know that he's a crazed gambler. The more vocal he is about it, the more cautious I must be.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I never imagined someone would share his way of thinking. Honestly, you should see a shrink.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Bring it. The box containing Cornerstone is unique, and only IPC senior staff and related members can access it — but I happen to be among them.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: I appreciate it.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Unfortunately, your guess is correct.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Ha, the golden stone. Its color and glow are similar to that of Qlipoth's body.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: This is the very ruse he intends to use to fool you. He won't reveal to you that the Ten Stonehearts chisel their own will into the Cornerstones, granting them an unparalleled radiance.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: And this golden stone is also known as a topaz, not aventurine, and it belongs to {RUBY_B#One of the Ten Stonehearts}Topaz{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: So? Do you wish to confront him?
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Not at the moment. I'm more interested to know the location of his Cornerstone.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: The safest place, somewhere you'd never think of. Because he never intended to hide it — in fact, that Cornerstone has been in your hands from the very beginning.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: I see, this bag... Mixing a Cornerstone, more precious than life itself, with a bunch of worthless jewels, disguised as a gift of money waiting to be confiscated, is indeed in line with {RUBY_B#Gambler}Mr. Aventurine{RUBY_E#}'s style.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Then he makes up some trivial excuse, downplaying the matter, and requests the gift money. This is a gamble, one he's all too familiar with, betting on your single misstep leading to a total loss.
rows.speaker: Dr. Ratio

rows.text: Learned Doctor, I'm grateful for your help. The Family will surely reward a righteous person like you.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: As for the villain... I hope he retreats in humiliation.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: It was all thanks to your friend with a keen eye that I could add a blot of utter failure to your storied career.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Ratio, you wretch...
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Finally shown your true colors, heh. Oh, and just to remind you: You currently only have seventeen system hours left to live. Treasure your remaining time, and savor the delectable aftertaste of defeat.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: ...You might as well explain yourself a little more clearly.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: What I performed on you just now was the Harmony's consecration. You were to show allegiance beneath the illumination of THEIR grace, yet you acted willfully, uttering nothing but falsehoods, transforming the consecration into a trial. I genuinely see no reason to absolve you from it.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Is this what the Harmony represents? Is it built upon constraint and coercion?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: You misunderstand, Mr. Aventurine. Punishment is meant for the irreverent, but I have seen your resilient spirit, and thus I offer you the possibility of a new beginning.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Throughout these seventeen system hours, you will be unable to escape the Dreamscape or contact any of your companions. You only have two paths before you, and it all depends on whether you can complete my test within the time limit.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Should you succeed, you will be able to coalesce into the Harmony and be with your Family. If you fail, you will suffer the wrath of the {RUBY_B#Embodiment of Harmony}Eternal Centurion{RUBY_E#} and fall into an abyss of doom.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Sounds like I'm going to end up the same either way.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: I indeed do need a servant to help me uncover the evil hidden in The Family from an external perspective. I will purge the evil from the inside and bring the real culprits to justice within seventeen system hours.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: When the time comes, compare your findings with mine. If both our findings align, or if you can provide me more insights... then THEY will truly be able to grant you mercy and honesty.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Shameless hypocrites... You took everything from me and still demand the truth? That isn't fair. Your carnival reeks with the stench of cash. Nothing is achievable without it!
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: This is meant to be an act of personal virtue, not requiring The Family's support. Your bag is over there, do as you please. I believe you can trade this bag of worthless jewels for everything you need. That's what gamblers excel at, isn't it?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Ah!
rows.speaker: Oak Family Soldier

rows.text: After screaming, the soldier collapses — he didn't even have time to earn a five-star rating from you.
Off you go, Mr. Aventurine. You are free. I will wait here for your good news.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: This meeting isn't an interrogation, or a negotiation...
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: It's an outright execution.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Why would I do that, Mr. Aventurine? I'm just wondering what a passerby who stumbled upon a scene of murder could have found out, that's all.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: By the way, before you go, I have a personal question.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: What is it now?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: You...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: ...Do you truly wish to bring about the destruction of this world?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Kakavasha, where did you go... Are you injured!?
I got it back, Sister.
rows.speaker: Kakavasha

rows.text: You went to look for them...? That's too dangerous! It's just a necklace. It's neither food nor water. We can survive without it.
But I can't live without you, little brother... Promise me not to look for those {RUBY_B#Shellslasher}Katicans{RUBY_E#} again, okay?
Sister, don't be afraid. The Katicans are fools, but I'm smart. I played a "game" with them, and I won.
rows.speaker: Kakavasha

rows.text: Won? What happened exactly? Tell me.
I made a bet with them — the two birds in the desert and me, who will die first? I won.
rows.speaker: Kakavasha

rows.text: They suspected me of cheating, but I didn't... I won fair and square.
rows.speaker: Kakavasha

rows.text: Of course. Of course you'd win... You've always been a lucky child. {RUBY_B#Fenge Biyos}Gaiathra Triclops{RUBY_E#} must be watching over you...
But that's no reason to push your luck by going up against those... those bloodthirsty, CRUEL Katicans! Have you forgotten how Mom and Dad...!
Look, this is just a necklace. But Kakavasha, you are my only family.
I'm sorry, Sister... I thought you'd be happy. Because mom left you this necklace...
rows.speaker: Kakavasha

rows.text: ...There'll be no next time.
rows.speaker: Kakavasha

rows.text: It is important, but not as important as you, my dearest brother... I don't blame you, but you must remember what mom said...
Pain and poverty are the trials of Gaiathra Triclops. She has also granted us a chance, and that's your good luck, Kakavasha. Your good luck is the most precious wealth we — all Avgin have.

You're a child blessed by {RUBY_B#Kakavasha}Gaiathra Triclops{RUBY_E#} and can lead the clan to happiness. So, always remember to protect yourself and never resent the pain and poverty you're going through... All right?
Listen to me, and swear to Gaiathra Triclops.
...Okay. I will swear to Gaiathra Triclops to protect this "wealth"...
rows.speaker: Kakavasha

rows.text: But Sister... If Gaiathra Triclops was really watching over us...
rows.speaker: Kakavasha

rows.text: Then why did she not protect Dad when he was swept away by the quicksand...? After all, Dad went to the Katicans' land only to prepare for Gaiathra Triclops' offerings...
rows.speaker: Kakavasha

rows.text: And where was Gaiathra Triclops when Mom was shivering in our arms? Mom was still pleading for Gaiathra Triclops' forgiveness under her breath until the moment she closed her eyes...
rows.speaker: Kakavasha

rows.text: Sister, everyone praises me for being smart, but I don't get it... If every rainpour was Gaiathra Triclops' forgiveness and grace...
rows.speaker: Kakavasha

rows.text: Then how bad were our sins? ...So much so that we were born in this world of death...?
rows.speaker: Kakavasha

rows.text: I don't know.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Interesting. Now, the final question...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "Can you swear that at this very moment, the Aventurine stone is safe and sound in this box?"
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: The two return to the lobby...
System hours ago — Dewlight Pavilion
Umm, excuse me...
rows.speaker: Alley

rows.text: I can't seem to find any information on this artist in the Iris Family archives. The photo you provided also doesn't show any matches...
rows.speaker: Alley

rows.text: ...Just as I thought. I'd like to ask, what kind of traces do people leave when they enter a dream?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Are you referring to the records when you enter the Dreampool? The equipment will monitor physiological indicators such as heart rate, blood oxygen levels, and body temperature in real time. This data will be included in statistics and handed over to The Family for the screening of any data anomalies. Immediate action will be taken once any illegal behavior is detected.
rows.speaker: Alley

rows.text: Please rest assured. Your vitals are monitored in case of emergencies, allowing us to wake you if necessary. This is all for the safety of our guests.
rows.speaker: Alley

rows.text: Can I trouble you to access the records?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I apologize... The hotel does not have access. This information is managed by the Bloodhound Family. We can only gain access if there's a problem.
rows.speaker: Alley

rows.text: Looks like nothing can be found here.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: At least we know who to look for next. We can ask the Bloodhound Family for information.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Thank you for your assistance, Miss Alley. By the way... is Miss Robin doing fine? We are looking forward to her performance.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Sorry, no can do. The boss said that since it's a matter of The Family's reputation, no one's allowed through.
rows.speaker: Principled Bloodhound Family Member

rows.text: Everyone, please leave. There's really no need for us to make things difficult for each other, right?
rows.speaker: Principled Bloodhound Family Member

rows.text: You and this Bloodhound Family member have met before, and you know he's very upright. But you're also aware that principles sometimes don't matter when a person is in a good mood.
If that's the case... I'll just have to acquiesce to everyone's wishes, lower my esteemed head and plead with everyone...
rows.speaker: Principled Bloodhound Family Member

rows.text: No no no! No need! Standing is just fine. You don't need to do that...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: (Looks like he still doesn't want to budge an inch...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: The principled Bloodhound Family member is mired in endless sorrow. As compensation, you have to think of a way to comfort him.

"Fine"... What does that mean? Is there something wrong with Miss Robin? The preparations for the Charmony Festival have been proceeding smoothly, so I guess things are pretty good. I believe she will be able to put on a spectacular show for all of you.
rows.speaker: Alley

rows.text: Mm, I'm sure.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Sure enough, no one knows about Miss Robin. I'm not surprised.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: But that Miss Firefly is truly mysterious. There's no information on her in the hotel system. Even if she's a stowaway... she should have a disguised identity after entering the planet.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: She's also in the running for the Legacy... How is she going to sneak into the Dreamscape unnoticed?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Is there any other way to enter a dream besides the hotel room's Dreampool?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The Memokeepers have abilities that are difficult for normal people to comprehend. In the Memory Zone of Penacony, they thrive effortlessly, a fact proven to us by Black Swan.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The hacker girl from the Stellaron Hunters used extraordinary means to unlock the dreamscape Hotel's seal. According to the scene witnessed by [Trailblazer], it is likely that they are behind Miss Firefly's case.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The Garden of Recollection... and the Stellaron Hunters, both are possible. But what about the IPC? Since they want Penacony all for themselves, they're bound to have a plan.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Wh—Who are you guys?
rows.speaker: Nervous Guest

rows.text: The Bravo team has arrived at their designated position. Ready to execute armed evacuation operation — boys, get moving!
Ar—armed evacuation? Boss, are you drunk?
What do you know!? It's more efficient this way. Just don't let the director find out! Act first, report later, understood?
Help... Help me... I spent all my year-end bonus on the snowball... I don't want my name on the department's major disciplinary notice!
Hey, [Trailblazer], check it out! That voice... Could it be the IPC Workers from Belobog?
